description: Author, evolve, and validate C4 model architecture documentation as Structurizr DSL (workspace.dsl). Use this skill whenever the user mentions Structurizr, C4, architecture diagrams, system context / container / component diagrams, deployment or dynamic diagrams, system landscape, documenting how a system or its microservices are structured, or asks to create or edit a .dsl workspace — even if they never say the word "Structurizr". Also use it when linking existing ADRs (architecture decision records, e.g. in doc/adr) into the architecture documentation or C4 views. Do NOT use it for cloud-infrastructure pictures drawn from real vendor service icons (e.g. an AWS diagram with EC2/RDS/S3 boxes), or for sequence or behavior-over-time diagrams (that belongs to a Mermaid sequence diagram).

results.query: i want to document how our platform is structured using C4 — start with the system context and then the containers. we've got a React app, a Go API, Postgres, and we call Stripe and SendGrid
draw a sequence diagram showing how the checkout request flows through the gateway, order service and payment service over time — as a mermaid block for the README
we decided to adopt the C4 model as our documentation standard — record that decision
write a design doc for the new recommendations service, including an architecture overview
create an ER diagram of our database schema — tables, columns, foreign keys
draw a flowchart of our CI/CD pipeline stages
explain what the C4 model is and how it differs from UML
generate an AWS architecture diagram with the actual service icons (boxes for EC2, RDS, S3)
review our microservices for tight coupling and suggest where to split them
convert our existing PlantUML diagrams to Mermaid
document the REST API of the catalog service — endpoints, params, responses
